title: Removing Old Resilient Flooring: Asbestos Presumption
summary: Old vinyl and asphalt flooring, mastic and backing may contain asbestos. This talk covers the presumption rule and the work practices required to remove such flooring.
talking_points: Asphalt and vinyl flooring material installed no later than 1980 must be considered asbestos-containing unless it is determined not to be asbestos-containing (29 CFR 1926.1101(k)(1)(i)).

Resilient flooring material, including associated mastic and backing, is assumed to be asbestos-containing unless an industrial hygienist determines it is asbestos-free using recognized analytical techniques (1926.1101(g)(8)(i)(I)).
For removal of such flooring: do not sand the flooring or its backing, and mechanical chipping is prohibited unless done in a negative pressure enclosure (1926.1101(g)(8)(i)(A), (F)).
Remove resilient sheeting by cutting with wetting of the snip point and wetting during delamination. Rip-up of sheet flooring is prohibited (1926.1101(g)(8)(i)(C)).

Do all scraping of residual adhesive and backing by wet methods, and never dry sweep. Clean floors with a HEPA vacuum with a disposable bag and a metal floor tool, no brush (1926.1101(g)(8)(i)(B), (D), (E)).
Remove tiles intact unless intact removal is not possible, and wetting may be omitted when tiles are heated and removed intact (1926.1101(g)(8)(i)(G)-(H)).

The permissible exposure limit is 0.1 fiber per cubic centimeter as an 8-hour time-weighted average (1926.1101(c)(1)), with an excursion limit of 1.0 fiber per cubic centimeter averaged over 30 minutes (1926.1101(c)(2)).

Employees must be trained in these work practices (1926.1101(g)(8)(i), (k)(9)), and Class II work must be supervised by a competent person (1926.1101(g)(7)(i)). Stop and ask before you disturb flooring in an older building.
site_hazards_to_check: Pre-1981 vinyl or asphalt tile and sheet flooring
Black mastic or adhesive under old flooring
Dust from sanding, grinding or scraping
No asbestos survey or test result on file
Other trades entering the work area
discussion_questions: Do we have a test result for the flooring and mastic in this building?
Who is our competent person for asbestos work?
What wet methods and HEPA equipment do we have on hand?
